# F5ZP R07 — axial approach connection repair

Status: EXPERIMENTAL; geometric repair against the recovered R05 trial reference. Not an approved cathedral revision. R07 is a new isolated version; R06 was not inspected or adopted.

## Open for review

Open `F5ZP_AXIAL_CONNECTION_R07_EXPERIMENTAL.blend` in Blender 4.3 or newer, or `F5ZP_AXIAL_CONNECTION_R07_ROOF_OFF.glb` in a GLB viewer. The full export includes the existing chapel roof. The roof-off export keeps the new approach webs visible. `R07_JUNCTION_CUTAWAY.png` hides the south approach web for inspection; those webs remain present in the files. Exhibit was not available, so inspection used Blender renders, a saved Blender reopen and an actual GLB import.

## Baseline and recovered evidence

- Supplied R05 diagnostic, QA, GLB and findings identify the two rear plan bearings at X25382.509765625, Y +/-1098.813232421875.
- Read GitHub `cathedral/governance/CATHEDRAL_MASTER_REFERENCE.md`, branch `cathedral/governance-r01`, blob `1d7e358ff7562fcc64088854baa2abd3d31a729e`. This remains a provisional governance register.
- Recovered the actual R03 `build_chapel.py`, `BASELINE.json` and parent QA from MR.COMPUTER. Script SHA256 `20f4829794624a6fa72f65663ee93c49225959eaa047256bfe685c12730cee5c`; baseline SHA256 `066027d5fa0e673b5c267718e906d105c86272b6358fcc8bf2a33a5d3fa92a19`. Both exactly match the supplied R05 source hashes.
- The attached Blender file is Blender 5.0 and could not be opened by the local Blender 4.3.2. It was inspected read-only on MR.COMPUTER with Blender 5.0.1. For portable output, reproduced the unchanged R03 source in Blender 4.3.2, then isolated the approach revision. This is not a rebuilt ambulatory generator.
- Recovered all 89 POLY control points of `F5ZN_A_FORMERET_R5285_BAY4_TRUE_POINTED` from the actual R05 Blender file. Retained its existing exported reference mesh. Its own properties explicitly label it as a trial envelope, not the original V13 rib curve.
- Native 1:1 coordinates: X east, Y north, Z up. Physical metres per native unit remain unresolved. No scale factor was applied; no Minecraft-grid conversion was introduced.

## Applied delta

| Relationship | Before | R07 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Rear spring Z | 1800 | 3000 |
| Rear boundary crown Z | 3500 | 4137.271484375, actual saved shared path |
| Approach boss | (26700,0,3620) | (26000,0,4400) |
| Front spring Z | 1800 | 1800, unchanged |
| Entrance back crown Z | 3923.328219... | unchanged |
| Entrance soffit crown Z | 3750 | unchanged |
| Threshold X range | 28000–28600 | unchanged |
| Chapel bay X ranges | 28600–31000; 31000–33400 | unchanged |

Removed the redundant low rear arch from the visible candidate and used the retained upper arch as the single rear web boundary. Replaced the four approach ogives and their matching vertical responds. They use monotone circular branches with exact vertical spring tangents; radii, centers and endpoints are recorded in QA. Moved/raised the boss because the old boss could not accept those branches from Z3000. Added two unequal-circle side arches with crests at X26000/Z4200 and five connected 45-unit web panels. Reused the original designed R03 section; no historical profile attribution is claimed. Extended the two existing trial rear cores to Z3000, retaining their footprints; normals of these copied cores were corrected.

All superseded approach meshes are retained in the hidden `R03_SUPERSEDED_APPROACH_HIDDEN` collection. Existing chapel bays, apse, roof, threshold, floor and source guides retain their mesh geometry and transforms. Presentation materials were configured for rendering. The protected ambulatory generator, F5ZK-C dimensions, Pass 6J and historical source files were not edited.

## Actual validation

- 231 unaffected source meshes retain identical vertex/face/transform fingerprints.
- Imported F5ZN trial reference mesh fingerprints unchanged through the repair.
- Five analytical web edge checks: maximum error 0.0 native units.
- Respond-to-rib section checks: maximum error 0.0.
- Saved rear mesh knots and unchanged threshold mesh knots meet exactly at checked vertices: maximum error 0.0 after Blender storage.
- All new generated meshes have zero nonmanifold edges, zero degenerate faces and positive enclosed signed volume.
- Each of the five new web panels has 69,696 intrados triangles; all projected triangle signs are consistent, with no projected folds.
- Full GLB round trip: 203 exported meshes, 203 imported; all names retained; overall world bounds error 0.0.
- Saved .blend reopened successfully. Two Blender renders and a measured SVG/PNG comparison inspected.
- Explicit test commands: `blender -b -t 4 --python build_R07.py`; `blender -b -t 2 --python verify_R07.py`.

These tests establish the recorded geometric fit and technical exports. They do not establish historical authenticity, a complete masonry bearing, or structural capacity. The preserved source chapel shell winding was outside this approach-only revision and was not newly certified. Intended assembly intersections are retained; this is not one boolean-unioned fabrication solid.

## Unresolved architecture

The revised approach is higher and has an offset boss. Its own roof and full main-cathedral/gallery/window clearance need coordinated development; source R03 did not have a roof over X25382–28000. No unverified roof or missing support schedule was invented. F5ZL-C support dimensions and structural capacity remain unresolved. Retaining the actual trial arch gives a tested interface to R05, not an independent verification of the approved F5ZN-A / original V13 authority. R07 must remain experimental pending architectural review.

## Reproduce from this package

Run `blender -b -t 4 --python build_R07.py`, then `blender -b -t 2 --python verify_R07.py`. Blender 4.3.2 was tested; its bundled NumPy is used. `inputs/R03_BASELINE.blend` is the unchanged source-script reproduction; `inputs/R05_INTERFACE.glb` is the supplied reference; path coordinates and section arrays are included. Original recovered source scripts, input baseline and parent QA are under `source_recovery`. `python draw_R07_comparison.py` regenerates the SVG/PNG with NumPy and Matplotlib. `render_R07.py` makes the optional wider workbench cutaway. Generated source paths/hashes are captured in numerical QA; hashes in `SHA256SUMS.json` validate packaged bytes.

def branch(A,B,label):

def sweep(name,f,sec=section,shaft=False):
